items.title: Finite-time blowup with compactly supported smooth force
items.paraphrase: For every viscosity there are a smooth force compactly supported in space and positive time and smooth compactly supported fields solving forced Navier-Stokes from rest on [0,1) with bounded energy and unbounded sup norm as t tends to 1, so no global smooth finite-energy solution exists for that force.
proofSteps: Build the concentrating axisymmetric leading profile (Theorem 4.6) and correct it to all orders into a base field with an annular stress residual (Proposition 5.5).
Add two families of shear-amplified, viscously damped waves whose averaged momentum flux cancels the leading stress (Lemma 7.4, Proposition 7.5, Lemma 7.7).
Run the four-operation correction cycle, gaining 1/10 in the residual exponent each time (Propositions 9.3, 9.5, 9.6).
Sum the corrections with shrinking cutoffs to get the local field with flat residual (Lemma 5.4, Proposition 9.9, Theorem 3.1).
Localise with space and time cutoffs and define the force as the residual (Proposition 10.1); extend it smoothly past t = 1 (Lemmas 10.2, 10.3).
Prove the energy and dissipation bounds (Lemma 10.4) and uniqueness against any finite-energy smooth solution (Lemma 10.5); the growth path then contradicts a global solution.
Rescale to arbitrary viscosity (Section 10.4).
